newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-MMC to cease Australia truck assembly.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-MMC to cease Australia truck assembly.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motors Australia Ltd (MMAL) said on Tuesday it would cease the assembly of trucks in Australia from the beginning of October 1997.

"Unfortunately the economics of the semi knock down (SKD) operation which is used to assemble trucks is no longer viable and is the reason we have reluctantly taken this decision," managing director Mike Quinn said in a statement.
A spokesman said Mitsubishi assembled about 2,000 trucks in a variety of models in 1996, with total annual sales of 2,130.
MMAL is wholly-owned by Mitsubishi Motors Corp.
Quinn said Mitsubishi, the second highest truck volume seller in Australia, had decided to follow most other truck makers which had already resorted to full imports.

The 40 people employed in Mitsubishi's Adelaide truck assembly area would be absorbed into its manufacturing operation to help it keep pace with strong orders for the Magna, Verada and export Diamante range, he said.

South Australian Premier John Olsen said in a separate statement the fall in tariffs on fully imported trucks, to five percent in 1996 from 20 percent in 1988, had no doubt played a part in Mitsubishi's decision.
But it was clear low volumes had also affected the viability of the SKD operations, he added.
